records.gloss: A psalm of David, when he was in [the] wilderness of Judah.
pieces: A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.

L.1: A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.

R.1: A song of David, from the time when he was in the desert of Judah.

decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: David in the wilderness of Judah
decisions.reason: David stayed in the wilderness of Judah while Saul hunted him (1 Samuel 23:14), and fled toward the wilderness again when Absalom rebelled (2 Samuel 15:23-28). Verse 12, which speaks of "the king", may fit the second time better.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Judah: dry hill country
decisions.reason: The land east of Judah's hills, falling toward the Dead Sea, is dry and rocky, with little water. It gives the picture of thirst in verse 2.
As in 3:1.

records.heading: Thirsting for God in a dry land

records.source: אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀אֵלִ֥י אַתָּ֗ה אֲֽשַׁחֲ֫רֶ֥ךָּ צָמְאָ֬ה לְךָ֨׀נַפְשִׁ֗י כָּמַ֣הּ לְךָ֣ בְשָׂרִ֑י בְּאֶֽרֶץ־צִיָּ֖ה וְעָיֵ֣ף בְּלִי־מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: God, my God [are] you; I seek you earnestly; it thirsts for you, my soul; it longs for you, my flesh, in a land of dryness and weary, without water.
pieces: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my God, and I search hard for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q My whole self thirsts for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; my body aches for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} \q in a dry and worn-out land with no water.

L.2: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] my God; I seek {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} earnestly; \q my soul thirsts for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; my flesh longs for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} \q in a dry and weary land, without water.

R.2: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my God. I want to be with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} more than anything. \q My whole body longs for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q like a traveler in a dry, tired land with no water anywhere.

decisions.reason: The verb (shachar) is related to the word for dawn, and some take it as "I look for you at dawn"; its usual sense is to seek eagerly (78:34; Proverbs 8:17).

decisions.choice: my soul, my flesh: my whole being
decisions.reason: Soul and flesh together mean the whole person, inner and outer (84:3).

decisions.choice: in a dry land: where he is, and what it is like
decisions.reason: The title places the psalmist in the wilderness; the dry land is both where he is and a picture of how he longs for God (42:2-3; 143:6).

decisions.choice: My whole self (B); My whole body (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable render nefesh by a phrase for the whole person (m2).

records.source: כֵּ֭ן בַּקֹּ֣דֶשׁ חֲזִיתִ֑יךָ לִרְא֥וֹת עֻ֝זְּךָ֗ וּכְבוֹדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: So in the sanctuary I have seen you, to see your strength and your glory.
pieces: So I have gazed on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in the holy place \q and seen {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} might and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory.

L.3: So in the sanctuary I have looked on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q to see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory.

R.3: I have seen {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy house. \q I have seen how strong and glorious {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

decisions.reason: The word links the longing of verse 2 with what the psalmist once saw in the sanctuary: he longs for God as he has known him there.

decisions.choice: I have seen you: met with God in worship
decisions.reason: To see God in the sanctuary is to know his presence in worship (27:4; 42:3), not to see a form.

records.gloss: For better [is] your loyal love than life; my lips will praise you.
pieces: Your loyal love is worth more than life, \q so my lips will sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.

L.4: For better [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love than life; \q my lips will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.4: Your faithful love means more to me than being alive. \q I will speak {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.

decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment that does not give up (5:8).
The verb (shabach) means to praise or commend (117:1).
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: כֵּ֣ן אֲבָרֶכְךָ֣ בְחַיָּ֑י בְּ֝שִׁמְךָ אֶשָּׂ֥א כַפָּֽי׃
records.gloss: So I will bless you in my life; in your name I will lift up my palms.
pieces: So I will bless {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all my life; \q I will raise my hands as I call on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.

L.5: So I will bless {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in my life; \q in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name I will lift up my palms.

R.5: All my life I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q I will raise my hands in prayer to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.reason: Raising open hands was a gesture of prayer and praise (28:2; 1 Kings 8:22).
When people bless God they praise him and give him thanks (34:2).

records.source: כְּמ֤וֹ חֵ֣לֶב וָ֭דֶשֶׁן תִּשְׂבַּ֣ע נַפְשִׁ֑י וְשִׂפְתֵ֥י רְ֝נָנ֗וֹת יְהַלֶּל־פִּֽי׃
records.gloss: As [with] fat and fatness it will be satisfied, my soul, and [with] lips of joyful shouts it will praise, my mouth.
pieces: I will be filled as with a feast of rich food, \q and with shouts of joy on my lips my mouth will sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.

L.6: As [with] fat and fatness my soul will be satisfied, \q and [with] lips of joyful shouts my mouth will praise [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}].

R.6: I will be satisfied, as if I had eaten the best food at a feast. \q I will sing for joy and praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: fat and fatness: the richest food
decisions.reason: Fat was the best part of a meal and of a sacrifice; the words mean a rich feast (36:9). Being with God satisfies like a banquet, in contrast to the thirst of verse 2.
Balanced and Readable say "I" for nefesh, as the convention allows.
The verb has no object; God is the one praised.

records.gloss: When I remember you on my beds, in [the] night watches I meditate on you,
pieces: When I call {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to mind as I lie in bed, \q I muse on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} through the hours of the night.

L.7: When I remember {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on my bed, \q in the night watches I meditate on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.7: When I lie in bed, I remember {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q I think about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all night long.

decisions.choice: the night watches: the long hours of the night
decisions.reason: The night was divided into three watches (Judges 7:19; Lamentations 2:19). The psalmist lies awake through them, thinking of God.
As in 1:2, the verb (hagah) is used of quiet speaking and thinking.

records.source: כִּֽי־הָיִ֣יתָ עֶזְרָ֣תָה לִּ֑י וּבְצֵ֖ל כְּנָפֶ֣יךָ אֲרַנֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: for you have been help to me, and in [the] shadow of your wings I shout for joy.
pieces: You have come to my help, \q and under the shadow of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wings I sing out for joy.

L.8: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been help to me, \q and in the shadow of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wings I shout for joy.

R.8: You have helped me. \q I am safe under {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} care, like a chick under its mother's wings, so I sing for joy.

decisions.choice: the shadow of your wings: God's protecting care
like a chick under its mother's wings
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1).

records.source: דָּבְקָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֣י אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ בִּ֝֗י תָּמְכָ֥ה יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: It clings, my soul, after you; on me it holds, your right hand.
pieces: I hold fast to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand keeps me safe.

L.9: My soul clings after {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand holds me fast.

R.9: I stay close to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hold me up with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong hand.

decisions.choice: clings after you: follows close behind you
decisions.reason: The verb (davaq) means to stick close, as Ruth clung to Naomi (Ruth 1:14); with "after" it is following closely.

decisions.choice: your right hand: God's strong help
decisions.reason: As in 18:36.
Balanced and Readable say "I" for nefesh, as the convention allows.

records.source: וְהֵ֗מָּה לְ֭שׁוֹאָה יְבַקְשׁ֣וּ נַפְשִׁ֑י יָ֝בֹ֗אוּ בְּֽתַחְתִּיּ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And they — to ruin they seek my soul; they will go into [the] lower parts of the earth.
pieces: But those who hunt my life to ruin it \q will sink into the lowest places of the earth.

L.10: But they — to [its] ruin they seek my soul; \q they will go into the lower parts of the earth.

R.10: But the people who want to kill me \q will go down into the grave.

decisions.choice: the lower parts of the earth: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: The deep places under the earth are where the dead go (86:13; Ezekiel 26:20).
Balanced and Readable say "my life" for nefesh, as the convention allows.

alternatives: the lower parts of the earth
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means (m1).

records.gloss: They will pour him onto [the] hands of [the] sword; [the] portion of foxes they will be.
pieces: The sword will have them in its grip, \q and jackals will take them as their share.

L.11: They will give him over to the power of the sword; \q they will be a portion for jackals.

R.11: They will be killed in battle, \q and wild dogs will eat their bodies.

decisions.choice: they will pour him: each of them will be given over
decisions.reason: "They" is impersonal and "him" is each of the enemies; the sense is that the enemies will be handed over.
The word (shu'al) covers foxes and jackals; jackals feed on the dead (Lamentations 5:18). To be left unburied was a great disgrace.

decisions.choice: the hands of the sword: the power of the sword
decisions.reason: Hands stand for power (Jeremiah 18:21).
Balanced and Readable say it in the passive and the plural (m1).

records.source: וְהַמֶּלֶךְ֮ יִשְׂמַ֪ח בֵּאלֹ֫הִ֥ים יִ֭תְהַלֵּל כָּל־הַנִּשְׁבָּ֣ע בּ֑וֹ כִּ֥י יִ֝סָּכֵ֗ר פִּ֣י דֽוֹבְרֵי־שָֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: And the king will rejoice in God; he will boast, everyone who swears by him, for it will be stopped, [the] mouth of [those] speaking falsehood.
pieces: But the king will find his joy in God; \q all who take their oaths in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name will celebrate, \q while liars will have their mouths shut.

L.12: But the king will rejoice in God; \q everyone who swears by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will boast, \q for the mouth of those who speak falsehood will be stopped.

R.12: But the king will be glad because of God. \q All who make their promises in God's name will be proud and happy, \q and liars will be silenced.

decisions.reason: The psalmist speaks of himself as "the king", or the psalm was sung for the king. His joy is in God, not in his own power.

alternatives: swears by the king (loyal to him)
decisions.reason: To swear by God is to trust and honor him (Deuteronomy 6:13; Isaiah 65:16). "Him" could also be the king, by whose life people swore loyalty (compare Genesis 42:15); the nearer name is God.
As in 34:3.
Readable names God (m2).
